identity.notes: The local name carries a fragment of the serial number, so it survives an address change and is the better identity key. Whether the cameras use a public or a rotating address is not recorded; treat the address as a connection locator.

methods.notes: Name OR service, as ble_scan methods combine them. Identify the model by the longest matching prefix (insta360ctl orders its table longest first). The models that speak only architecture A (ONE X, ONE X2, ONE R) are found by name; what, if anything, they serve to a phone is not recorded.

host_compatibility.basis: insta360ctl's default backend is BlueZ D-Bus (bluetoothd's GATT client, via tinygo bluetooth), and its author reports photo, record, mode, battery, storage and GPS working against a GO 3. Which backend those runs used is not stated.
host_compatibility.notes: GPS-remote emulation needs the host to be a GATT server; insta360ctl requires its raw-HCI backend for that, not bluetoothd.

host_compatibility.basis: The vendor app and the official Android SDK connect to the cameras over BLE on Android (SDK README, connection module).

identification.notes: Cameras advertise "<model prefix><part of the serial number>", e.g. "X3 " followed by a serial fragment (insta360ctl's model table; the vendor app's string pool carries the same prefixes plus "X4 Air " and "Ace Pro 2 ", which the prefixes above also catch). The trailing space is part of each prefix and keeps "ONE R " from matching "ONE RS ". "X3 " and "Ace " are short enough to collide with unrelated products; rank a hit that also serves 0000be80-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb above one that does not. insta360ctl also falls back to a bare "ONE " prefix, left out here as too generic. The 0000be80-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb service UUID is on the Bluetooth base but is not a SIG assignment; the vendor app appears to scan with a filter on it (string-level evidence), so cameras probably advertise it, which nobody has confirmed. No company ID or OUI is documented. GO 2 and X6 name prefixes are unknown.

device.name: Insta360 360° and action cameras (X3/X4/X5, ONE X/X2/RS/R, Ace/Ace Pro, GO 2/GO 3)
device.notes:
Insta360 360-degree and action cameras from Arashi Vision (Shenzhen). One spec covers the family because every model speaks one of two BLE architectures, and most speak both. Which ones a model speaks is carried per model in device.variants and in protocol_details.model_matrix. Picking one architecture and generalising would be wrong for half the fleet.
TRANSPORTS. (1) BLE, for discovery, remote-style control and full direct control. (2) The camera's own Wi-Fi access point: gateway 192.168.42.1, SSID made of the model name, a space and a six-character serial fragment, ending ".OSC" on the ONE RS example Rigacci published. A proprietary TCP protocol on port 6666 multiplexes protobuf commands, replies, notifications, keep-alives and the live-preview stream. The camera can also be moved into station mode on the user's network; the same TCP protocol then runs on its DHCP address (protocol_details.wifi_tcp). (3) USB mass storage and UVC, out of scope. The SDK says BLE cannot carry bulk data: preview, file transfer and firmware updates need Wi-Fi or USB.
ARCHITECTURE A, GPS-REMOTE EMULATION. The roles are reversed: the HOST is the GATT server and advertises as an Insta360 GPS remote, and the camera connects to it as a central. The host serves service 0000ce80-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb (characteristics 0000ce81-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb that the camera writes, 0000ce82-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb that the host notifies commands on, and 0000ce83-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb, a static read) plus an information service 0000d0ff-3c17-d293-8e48-14fe2e4da212. Commands are fixed 9-byte frames FC EF FE 86 00 03 01 <action> <param>: shutter, mode cycle, screen, power off. A sleeping camera is woken by an iBeacon-shaped manufacturer-data advertisement that carries "ORBIT" and a six-character camera ID. Because the camera is the client, none of this is in `services` (which lists what the camera serves). It is all in protocol_details.gps_remote_emulation.
ARCHITECTURE B, DIRECT CONTROL. The camera is the GATT server. Commands go to 0000be81-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb and replies and events come back as notifications on 0000be82-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb, both under service 0000be80-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb. A message is a 16-byte header (7-byte packet head, 9-byte message head) followed by a protobuf body. The 16-byte form is byte-for-byte the packet the TCP/6666 protocol uses, with its uint32 length prefix. On the GO line the message is wrapped in a 5-byte envelope (FF 07 40 + uint16 LE size, or FF 07 41 for sync) and a CRC-16/MODBUS trailer, little-endian; packets are at most 500 bytes and longer messages arrive over several notifications and are reassembled by the size field. The GO 3 also serves a secondary service 0000b000-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb with four characteristics, but only listens on 0000be81-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb. Session setup on the GO line: the camera sends a sync frame after the first write and the client answers with its own; then CHECK_AUTHORIZATION (0x27); if the camera says not authorized, REQUEST_AUTHORIZATION (0x56), which the user approves on the camera, the verdict arriving as notification 0x2011. After that the client sends message codes from the vendor's table: photo (3), record start/stop (4/5), highlight (60), GPS (53), Wi-Fi station hand-off SET_WIFI_CONNECTION_INFO (112) whose outcome and new IP address arrive as notification 8232 (0x2028).
FRAMING IS NOT SETTLED FOR THE X, ONE AND ACE MODELS. insta360ctl assumes they take the 16-byte header bare, with no envelope, no sync and no authorization, and with bytes 0-1 holding the payload length. It never ran that path on hardware. Two things argue against it: the vendor's own packet convention (TCP and the GO envelope) puts the TOTAL length, header included, in bytes 0-3, so the bare form's length field disagrees by 16; and the official SDK, which supports only X- and ONE-series cameras, reports BLE "sync pack" and "shake hand" errors, so those cameras almost certainly sync too. Both candidate forms are declared (the `framed_*` and `bare_*` commands) and the question is recorded in remaining_unknowns. The GO-line framed form is the one with upstream hardware results.
CLIENT RULES that hold on every source:
  1. Subscribe to 0000be82-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb (and to 0000b002-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb, 0000b003-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb and 0000b004-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb on service 0000b000-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb where it exists) before writing.
  2. Write commands to 0000be81-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb only. The GO 3 ignores the same frames on 0000b001-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb and 0000ae01-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb.
  3. On the GO line, answer the camera's sync frame at once or every later command is silently dropped.
  4. Sequence numbers run 1-254 and wrap; 0 and 255 are reserved. Match replies by sequence. Replies carry an HTTP-style status in the code field (200, 400, 500, 501). Notifications carry codes of 0x2000 and up; dispatch them by code, not by sequence.
  5. Reuse one authorization_id per client. A new one makes the camera ask the user again (inferred from the flow).
  6. Never send a code for a meaning its official name does not have. insta360ctl sends several "legacy" codes on models whose firmware may read them as something else, including 0x0C, which the vendor table names DELETE_FILES, to set the capture mode (protocol_details.direct_control.misattributed_codes).

SDK CREDENTIALS. The official SDK's camera activation needs an appId and secretKey that a developer applies to Insta360 for; activation is an online call that the vendor rate-limits and region-checks. That is the credentials' whole role here: the community protocol paths in this spec need neither, and no key is recorded. Rigacci reports the vendor app was needed to activate his ONE RS on first use; whether an un-activated camera refuses any of the local protocol is not established.
CROSS-CHECKS FROM THE VENDOR APP'S STRING POOL (2.33.0). It carries 0000be80-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb, 0000ce80-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb to 0000ce83-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb, 0000ffd0-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb to 0000ffd5-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb and 0000ffd8-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb (all on the Bluetooth base), 0000d0ff-3c17-d293-8e48-14fe2e4da212 and 000002fd-3c17-d293-8e48-14fe2e4da212 on the vendor base, the name prefixes, "syNceNdinS", 88888888, 192.168.42.1, http://192.168.42.1:80, the ten wake-beacon bytes 09 4f 52 42 49 54 09 ff 0f 00, and a complete GO-envelope heartbeat frame whose CRC our transcription of the algorithm reproduces. An earlier research note that the pool also holds camera ports 8080 and 9999 did not survive a re-check (protocol_details.wifi_tcp.other_ports).

openness.notes: Insta360 publishes a camera SDK, but only as binary libraries handed out on application, with online camera activation that needs an appId and a secretKey issued by Insta360, and (per Rigacci) a licence that forbids mixing it with open-source software. The wire protocol under it is not published. Everything below the API level was recovered by the community (insta360ctl, pchwalek, Rigacci), so this spec is a reconstruction and can be wrong.

enter_pairing_mode.notes: Direct control needs no pairing mode: the camera advertises while on, and a new client is admitted by the user approving the REQUEST_AUTHORIZATION prompt on the camera. For GPS-remote emulation the camera must presumably be told to pair with a remote from its own menus; no source documents the steps.

exclusivity.notes: The authorization flow has a "busy" outcome when another device is mid-authorization, and the SDK has "camera is occupied" (4403) and "device Bluetooth busy" (4508) errors, so the camera serves one controlling client at a time in practice; the link-layer limit is not recorded.
exclusivity.recovery: Close the vendor app and any other BLE client, then reconnect. If the camera still reports it is occupied, power-cycle it (GO 2: hold the Action button 6 s to force a shutdown).

pairing.notes: No link-layer pairing is demanded: insta360ctl connects to a GO 3 through bluetoothd without bonding and gets answers. The security lives one layer up. CHECK_AUTHORIZATION (0x27) carries a client-chosen authorization_id; an unknown ID gets 'not authorized', and REQUEST_AUTHORIZATION (0x56) then puts a prompt on the camera that the user must accept; the verdict comes back as notification 0x2011. The sources disagree on the status numbering (insta360ctl's prose table says 1 = not authorized, 3 = authorized; its code, which ran against a GO 3, uses 1 = authorized, 2 = not authorized), and on whether the X, ONE and Ace models authorize at all (insta360ctl skips it for them). Whether the camera also requests a bond when a central offers one is not recorded. There is also a separate wake-up authorization frame for a sleeping camera (protocol_details.direct_control.wake_up_authorization).

unpair.notes: The vendor table has CANCEL_AUTHORIZATION (40, 0x28), which may revoke a client's approval; no open implementation sends it (insta360ctl misuses 0x28 as a "get device info" code), and no camera-side menu for approved clients is documented.

security_advisory.detail: Rigacci's 2023 write-up on a ONE RS reports that the camera's access point at 192.168.42.1 comes up with the factory passphrase 88888888, that he found no way to disable it or change the passphrase from the camera, and that anyone who joins it can telnet into the camera's Linux system as root and, in his words, do anything up to damaging the camera permanently. insta360ctl notes that some firmware versions use a random passphrase instead, and the vendor SDK exposes a "password version" beside the passphrase, so newer firmware may differ. The passphrase string 88888888 is also in the current vendor app's string pool. Which models and firmware versions are affected is not established. This spec does not document the shell. Keep the camera's Wi-Fi off when you are not using it.
security_advisory.summary: The camera's own Wi-Fi access point used the fixed passphrase 88888888 on at least the ONE RS, and a root telnet shell was reported reachable through it.

credentials.notes: The camera issues nothing to the client. The client chooses its own authorization_id and must keep reusing it. The station-mode passphrase crosses BLE or TCP as a plain protobuf string with no encryption above the link, and the camera AP passphrase can be read back over both (SDK Wi-Fi info; GET_OPTIONS option 36 over TCP).
stored_on_device: The camera AP's SSID and passphrase (88888888 on older firmware; per-unit on some newer firmware).
Station-mode networks and passphrases handed over with SET_WIFI_CONNECTION_INFO; the camera keeps a list (GET_CONNECTED_WIFI_LIST, DEL_WIFI_HISTORY_INFO).
The authorization IDs of BLE clients the user approved (inferred: CHECK_AUTHORIZATION answers 'authorized' for a known ID).

factory_reset.description: No source run for this spec documents a factory reset, and the two user-manual exhibits (GO 3 quick guide, GO 2 manual) cover only power and capture buttons; the GO 2 manual's 6-second hold of the Action button is a forced shutdown, not a reset. The vendor message table does contain RESTORE_FACTORY_SETTINGS (code 57, 0x39), so a protocol-level reset exists, but no open implementation sends it. A separate code RESET_WIFI (125, 0x7D) exists; the SDK's matching call is documented as restarting the camera's Wi-Fi (off, then on), not as erasing credentials.
factory_reset.effect: Not established. The camera stores its AP credentials, any station-mode networks, the IDs of authorized BLE clients and its settings; nothing documents which of these a reset clears.

procedures.basis: The vendor's message-code table as transcribed by insta360ctl (doc/ble_protocol.md section 9.1). No open implementation sends it and its effect is undocumented.
procedures.name: RESTORE_FACTORY_SETTINGS message (code 57, 0x39)

steps.action: Over an authorized BLE session or a synced TCP session, send a message with code 57 and an empty body.
steps.expect: Unknown. Presumably status 200 and a restart with default settings.

methods.description: Connect to the camera as a central, subscribe to its notify characteristic, complete the sync (GO line) and the authorization exchange, and send commands. The first time a client asks, the user approves it on the camera. The vendor app's scanner filters on this service (string-level evidence), and insta360ctl's GO 3 results rest on it. On the X, ONE and Ace models the framing is unsettled (device.notes): try the framed form with sync and authorization first, and fall back to insta360ctl's bare form.
methods.name: Direct control on the camera's own GATT service, approved once on the camera

steps.action: Power the camera on. It advertises '<model prefix><serial fragment>' while on; insta360ctl documents no other preparation.
Scan for a name prefix from device.identification, connect, and discover services.
Request a larger ATT MTU. The vendor app negotiates 247 (about 244 bytes per write); insta360ctl asks for 517. Without it, framed packets longer than 20 bytes must be split across writes.
Send CHECK_AUTHORIZATION (code 0x27) with a stable authorization_id string for this client (protocol_details.test_vectors.check_authorization).

GO line: the camera answers the first write with a sync frame (FF 06 41 ..., body a repeating AB BA). Write the sync reply (command framed_sync_reply: FF 07 41 07 00 + seven zero bytes + CRC) at once.
steps.expect: The camera then processes the pending CHECK_AUTHORIZATION and replies with status 200 and an authorization status. Without the sync reply, commands are silently dropped.

steps.action: If the status is 'not authorized', send REQUEST_AUTHORIZATION (code 0x56) with operation type 1 (pair).
Approve the connection on the camera when it asks (screen or button).
steps.expect: Notification 0x2011 (AUTHORIZATION_RESULT) with field 1 true. insta360ctl reads the verdict from the direct reply to 0x56 instead; accept either.

steps.action: Send commands (the framed_* commands on the GO line; see device.notes for the other models), one sequence number per message, 1-254.

timing.authorization_prompt_timeout_s: Not documented. The 60 s above is a client-side choice, not a device constant.
timing.heartbeat: The vendor app carries a BLE heartbeat frame (framed_heartbeat). How often it is sent, and whether the camera drops an idle link without it, is not recorded. The TCP equivalent is every 2 s.
timing.mtu: Vendor app 247; insta360ctl 517. Framed packets max 500 bytes.

causes: The frames went to 0000b001-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb or 0000ae01-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb. insta360ctl's real-device testing found the GO 3 answers only on 0000be81-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb.
The camera's sync frame was not answered. It arrives after the first write; reply with framed_sync_reply.
Notifications were not enabled before the first write.
troubleshooting.symptom: GO 3 accepts the connection but never answers commands.

causes: Another device is mid-authorization with the camera (the vendor's authorization states include busy).
Nobody approved the prompt on the camera in time, or it was declined. The SDK reports a refusal as error 4505, 'Bluetooth binding rejected'.
troubleshooting.symptom: Authorization fails with busy, timeout or denied.

causes: The vendor app or another client holds the camera. Close the app, disconnect other clients, and retry.
troubleshooting.symptom: The camera reports it is occupied, or the connection is refused (SDK errors 4403, 4508).

causes: Framing unsettled for these models (device.notes). Try the framed form with sync and authorization, then the bare form.
troubleshooting.symptom: An X-, ONE- or Ace-series camera ignores every command.

causes: insta360ctl sets the mode with code 0x0C and a raw mode byte. That works on the GO 3, but the vendor table names 0x0C DELETE_FILES. Do not send it to any other model (protocol_details.direct_control.misattributed_codes).
troubleshooting.symptom: The capture mode changed, or files may have been touched, after a 'set mode' from a community tool.

methods.description: Join the camera's own access point and speak the TCP protocol to 192.168.42.1:6666. Needs no BLE and no authorization exchange in either open implementation, but the host loses its internet connection while it is on the camera's network. Rigacci's working ONE RS client and the vendor SDK's Wi-Fi connection use this path; insta360ctl implements it but marks it untested.
methods.name: Camera Wi-Fi access point, TCP 6666 (nothing to provision)

softap.passphrase_source: 88888888 on older firmware (Rigacci, ONE RS; also in the vendor app's strings). Some firmware uses a random passphrase: read it in the camera's settings, over BLE (the SDK exposes SSID and passphrase once connected), or over TCP with GET_OPTIONS option 36 (payload_formats.Options_Wifi_Info).

steps.action: Turn the camera's Wi-Fi on (on the camera, or over BLE with OPEN_CAMERA_WIFI, code 33, which the SDK exposes as 'open camera Wi-Fi').
Join the camera's access point (SSID '<model> <6-character serial fragment>', '.OSC' suffix on the ONE RS example) with its passphrase.
Open a TCP connection to 192.168.42.1:6666 and send the sync packet 11 00 00 00 06 00 00 73 79 4e 63 65 4e 64 69 6e 53 (length 17, type 06 00 00, ASCII 'syNceNdinS').
steps.expect: The camera echoes the identical packet. insta360ctl treats no echo within 5 s as a failed connection.

steps.action: From now on send the keep-alive 07 00 00 00 05 00 00 whenever the link has been idle for 2 s.
steps.expect: The camera drops a client it has heard nothing from for about 10 s.

steps.action: Send commands as TCP message packets (protocol_details.wifi_tcp.message_packet). Rigacci's client first sets the camera's clock (SET_OPTIONS, code 7, local time and time zone).

timing.basis: insta360ctl doc/protocol.md and Rigacci's client (2 s keep-alive, 10 s receive timeout).

causes: The camera AP has no uplink. The SDK FAQ explains the vendor app binds its process to the camera network to reach the socket. Use station mode, or a second network interface, or bind only the camera socket to the camera network.
troubleshooting.symptom: The phone or computer has no internet while connected to the camera (a recurring store-review complaint about the vendor app).

causes: Rigacci saw this on the ONE RS: white balance, resolution and FOV changes take effect at the next capture but the on-screen labels and live view do not update. Sharpness, prompt sound and indicator LEDs could not be changed at all.
troubleshooting.symptom: Settings changed over TCP do not show on the camera's screen or preview.

causes: Rigacci: with the display asleep, GET_PHOTOGRAPHY_OPTIONS sometimes returns stale values; closing and reopening the socket restores them.
troubleshooting.symptom: A focal-length or FOV value read back does not match what was set.

methods.description: The host plays an Insta360 GPS remote: it advertises and serves the remote's GATT layout, and the camera connects as the central. Only shutter, mode cycle, screen and power off are available, plus waking a sleeping camera. It is the only BLE route documented for the ONE X, ONE X2 and ONE R, and it needs a host that can run a GATT server (insta360ctl needs raw HCI on Linux for it; pchwalek uses an ESP32). Everything is in protocol_details.gps_remote_emulation.
methods.name: GPS-remote emulation: the camera connects to the host

steps.action: Serve service 0000ce80-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb (0000ce81-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb write, 0000ce82-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb notify, 0000ce83-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb read) and service 0000d0ff-3c17-d293-8e48-14fe2e4da212 with the values in protocol_details.gps_remote_emulation.gatt_server.
Advertise the name 'Insta360 GPS Remote' with service UUIDs 0000ce80-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb and 0000d0ff-3c17-d293-8e48-14fe2e4da212 and a scan response.
Have the camera connect to the remote. No source documents the camera-side steps; the vendor GPS remote is paired from the camera's own menus (hypothesis).
steps.expect: The camera connects and enables notifications on 0000ce82-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb.

steps.action: Notify 9-byte commands on 0000ce82-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb, e.g. FC EF FE 86 00 03 01 02 00 for the shutter.
To wake a camera that has powered down, stop normal advertising and advertise the wake manufacturer data (protocol_details.gps_remote_emulation.wake_advertisement) with the camera's six-character ID.
steps.expect: A camera that has been paired with the remote powers on and reconnects (pchwalek: X3 and ONE RS 1-inch).

causes: The camera-side pairing step is not documented; the camera may only connect to a remote it has been paired with.
The host's stack cannot act as a peripheral with these services (bluetoothd-based clients generally cannot; insta360ctl switches to raw HCI).
troubleshooting.symptom: The camera never connects to the emulated remote.

methods.description: Tell the camera to leave its own AP and join an existing network, so a client on that LAN can reach TCP 6666 without switching networks. The command goes over an authorized BLE session (method 1) or over TCP on the camera AP (method 2). insta360ctl implements both and marks both untested; its notes say some models or firmware may not support station mode. The passphrase travels as a plain protobuf string.
methods.name: Station mode: hand the camera your network (SET_WIFI_CONNECTION_INFO, code 112)

steps.action: Open an authorized BLE session (method 1) or a synced TCP session on the camera AP (method 2).
Send SET_WIFI_CONNECTION_INFO (code 112) whose body is field 1 = { field 1 ssid, field 2 bssid (optional), field 3 passphrase } (protocol_details.test_vectors.set_wifi_connection_info).
steps.expect: Status 200: the command was accepted, not that the join worked.

steps.action: Wait for notification 8232 (0x2028): field 1 result (0 success, 1 timeout, 2 connect failed), field 2 the connection info with field 4 = the camera's new IP address.
steps.expect: On TCP the notification may arrive before or after the camera drops its AP and the socket; a drop after the 200 usually means the join worked.

steps.action: Connect to <new IP>:6666 and sync as in method 2. If no IP was reported, look the camera up in the router's DHCP leases.

causes: Wrong passphrase or an unsupported band/security mode: notification 8232 reports 2 (connect failed) or 1 (timeout).
The model or firmware does not support station mode (insta360ctl's caution).
troubleshooting.symptom: The camera accepts the command but never appears on the LAN.

causes: 0x1A is SCAN_BT_PERIPHERAL in the vendor table; insta360ctl's earlier builds misused it. The join is code 112.
troubleshooting.symptom: Wi-Fi join via code 0x1A from an older community build does nothing.

setup.notes: Nothing has to be provisioned for BLE control or for the camera's own Wi-Fi AP; the only one-time step is the user approving a new client on the camera the first time it asks for authorization (GO line; see device.pairing). Station mode is optional provisioning. Confidence is low because only the GO 3 direct-control flow has an upstream hardware result, the X/ONE/Ace framing is unsettled, and the camera-side steps for pairing a remote are not documented anywhere. First-use activation: Rigacci reports the vendor app had to activate his new ONE RS; the SDK does it online with developer credentials. Whether an un-activated camera limits the local protocol is not established.

rejoin.notes: Reported, untested: SET_WIFI_CONNECTION_INFO can be sent again over BLE at any time, so the camera can be handed a new network without a reset. The vendor table also has SET_WIFI_MODE (147; 0 AP, 1 station, 2 P2P), GET_CONNECTED_WIFI_LIST (149) and DEL_WIFI_HISTORY_INFO (175) for returning to AP mode and forgetting saved networks. Moving the camera to a new phone needs only a new BLE authorization.

steps.action: Over BLE, send SET_WIFI_CONNECTION_INFO (code 112) with the new network, or SET_WIFI_MODE (code 147) with mode 0 to go back to the camera's own AP.

testing.notes: Nobody on this project has driven an Insta360 camera from this document, and the research store holds no capture of one. Every fact is reported from the open implementations and the vendor SDK README, or from string-level evidence in the packed vendor app. The strongest upstream results, none of them ours: insta360ctl's author ran photo, record start/stop, mode, battery, storage and GPS injection against a GO 3 over direct control (its CLI marks everything else "not tested, yet"); pchwalek's sketch drove an X3 and a ONE RS 1-inch as a GPS-remote emulator, including the wake advertisement; Rigacci drove a ONE RS over TCP 6666 from a working remote-control program.

initialization.notes: Replies and notifications arrive only here. Subscribe before the first write.

initialization.description: GO line (and probably every direct-control model): after the first write the camera sends a sync frame on 0000be82-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb (FF 06 41, uint16 LE size, a repeating AB BA body, CRC). Answer it immediately with framed_sync_reply (FF 07 41 07 00, seven zero bytes, CRC 5C 42). A client must handle this whenever it arrives; it is event-driven, not a fixed write.

Authorization: CHECK_AUTHORIZATION (0x27) with the client's stable authorization_id and initiator type 2 (app); if the reply's status is not-authorized, REQUEST_AUTHORIZATION (0x56) with operation type 1 (pair), then wait for the user to approve on the camera and for notification 0x2011. The body carries a client-chosen string, so the bytes cannot be fixed here; protocol_details.test_vectors gives a worked example. insta360ctl performs this only on the GO line.

Authorization_Status.description: Field 1 of the reply to CHECK_AUTHORIZATION (0x27). insta360ctl's code, which ran against a GO 3, uses the numbering below; its prose table disagrees (1 = not authorized, 2 = pending, 3 = authorized). Treat anything but 1 as needing REQUEST_AUTHORIZATION until someone checks. Field 2 is a Find My pairing status, 0-2.

Framed_Packet.description: The GO-line BLE envelope around one inner packet (vendor native library, per insta360ctl; hardware-exercised on a GO 3; the vendor app's string pool carries two complete frames whose CRCs check).

fields.description: Byte 0: 0xFF.
fields.name: marker

fields.description: Byte 1: 0x07 on app-to-camera frames; 0x06 on the camera's frames (insta360ctl's constant and the app's 'ff0641'/'ff0640' strings). Other values (0x0C, 0x0D) belong to the short wake-up form.
fields.name: direction_type

fields.description: Byte 2: 0x40 message, 0x41 sync.
fields.name: packet_kind

fields.description: Bytes 3-4: uint16 little-endian, the number of inner bytes that follow (16 + body for a message).
fields.name: inner_size

fields.description: Bytes 5 .. 5+inner_size-1: the inner packet (payload_formats.Inner_Header) or sync data.
fields.name: inner

fields.description: Last 2 bytes: CRC-16/MODBUS (reflected poly 0xA001, init 0xFFFF, no final xor) over every earlier byte, little-endian.
fields.name: crc

parse_rules: Accumulate notifications until at least 5 bytes are buffered, read inner_size from bytes 3-4, then keep accumulating until 5 + inner_size + 2 bytes are buffered.
Verify the CRC over bytes 0 .. 5+inner_size-1 before using the frame; drop the frame on a mismatch.
Byte 2 = 0x41 is a sync frame: answer it with framed_sync_reply at once.
Otherwise parse the inner bytes with Inner_Header.
Frames are at most 500 bytes; messages that do not fit are split with the fragment fields of the inner header.

Go3_Battery_Reply.description: Body of the status-200 reply to code 25 on the GO 3 (framed_get_battery_go3). Protobuf varints.
Go3_Battery_Reply.example: 08 4b 10 00  (75 %, not charging; constructed from the documented fields)

fields.description: Field 1 (tag 0x08), battery level 0-100.
fields.name: level

fields.description: Field 2 (tag 0x10), 1 while charging, 0 otherwise.
fields.name: charging

Go3_Capture_Status.description: Body of notification 0x2010 as observed on the GO 3 (insta360ctl). Protobuf varints. Units of the capacity fields are not established.

fields.description: Field 1: 0 idle, 1 post-recording, 4 recording.
fields.name: capture_state

fields.description: Field 4: free capacity; unit not established (MB or remaining seconds).
fields.name: free_capacity

fields.description: Field 5: number of files.
fields.name: file_count

fields.description: Field 6: total capacity; unit not established.
fields.name: total_capacity

Inner_Header.description: The 16-byte inner header: a 7-byte packet head and a 9-byte message head. Identical, byte for byte, to a TCP/6666 packet including its length prefix.

fields.description: Bytes 0-3: total inner size including these 16 bytes (16 + body). insta360ctl's bare form writes the body length here instead.
fields.name: packet_size

fields.description: Byte 4: 0x04 message, 0x05 keep-alive/heartbeat, 0x06 sync, 0x01 stream (the TCP values; the BLE heartbeat uses 0x05).
fields.name: packet_type

fields.description: Bytes 5-6: 0x00 0x00 in every observed message.
fields.name: packet_flags

fields.description: Bytes 7-8: message code (app requests), status 200/400/500/501 (replies), or a notification code of 0x2000 and up.
fields.name: code

fields.description: Byte 9: 0x02 protobuf (0x00 raw).
fields.name: content_type

fields.description: Byte 10: sequence number 1-254 (the low byte of a 30-bit fragment offset field that spans bytes 10-13).
fields.name: sequence

fields.description: Byte 13: bit 7 last fragment, bit 6 direction (1 = camera to app), bits 0-5 upper fragment-offset bits. 0x80 on a single-fragment request, 0xC0 on a single-fragment reply.
fields.name: fragment_flags

fields.description: Bytes 14-15: zero in requests; non-zero values have been seen in replies over TCP (Rigacci), meaning unknown.
fields.name: trailer

Notification_Codes.description: Unsolicited camera messages, dispatched by code. Names from the vendor table as transcribed by insta360ctl; the GO 3 reuses some codes with different contents (protocol_details.direct_control.go3_deviations). Over TCP their sequence field is arbitrary (Rigacci saw ff 8a 43), so never route them by sequence.

values.8208: 0x2010 current capture status (GO 3: storage fields, see Go3_Capture_Status)
values.8225: 0x2021 GO 3 battery state (not in the vendor table)
values.8229: 0x2025 GO 3 power state (not in the vendor table)
values.8230: 0x2026 GO 3 periodic status (not in the vendor table)
values.8232: 0x2028 Wi-Fi connection result (station-mode join outcome and IP)

Options_Wifi_Info.description: Reply to GET_OPTIONS (code 8) asking for option type 36 (Wi-Fi info), from Rigacci's published ONE RS exchange. The reply body's field 1 repeats the option types asked for; field 2 holds one sub-field per option whose field number equals the option type (15 serial number, 36 Wi-Fi info, 48 camera type in Rigacci's example). Inside Wi-Fi info: field 1 SSID, field 2 passphrase, field 3 channel, field 4 unknown (0). The SDK reads the same information over BLE; that the BLE path uses this message is inferred.
parse_rules: Request body: field 1 = 36 (0a 01 24 packed, or 08 24; proto3 parsers accept both).
Reply body: skip field 1; in field 2 find field 36 (key bytes a2 02), and decode its sub-fields.

Remote_Command.description: Architecture A: the 9-byte frame the emulated remote notifies on 0000ce82-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb (pchwalek, insta360ctl).

fields.description: Bytes 0-6: FC EF FE 86 00 03 01, constant.
fields.name: preamble

fields.description: Byte 7: 0x00 screen/power group, 0x01 mode, 0x02 shutter.
fields.name: action

fields.description: Byte 8: 0x00 normally; with action 0x00, 0x03 = power off (0x00 = screen).
fields.name: param

Response_Status.description: The code field of a reply. The sequence number matches the request.

values.200: OK. The body is the reply message for the request's code (often empty).
values.400: Bad request: unknown code or invalid parameters. The body may carry an error message (protobuf field 2, string).
values.500: Execution error, e.g. 'camera is busy.' or 'msg execute err.' (Rigacci, ONE RS). Body: field 1 error code, field 2 message string.

fields.description: Field 1: 0 success, 1 timeout, 2 connect failed.
fields.name: result

fields.description: Field 2: field 1 ssid, field 2 bssid, field 3 passphrase, field 4 the camera's new IP address (dotted-quad string, set on success).
fields.name: connection_info

conflicts_between_sources.authorization_status_numbering: insta360ctl prose: 1 not authorized, 2 pending, 3 authorized, 4 expired, 5 denied. insta360ctl code (ran on a GO 3): 1 authorized, 2 not authorized, 3 pending, 4 denied, 5 expired.
conflicts_between_sources.authorization_verdict: insta360ctl prose: the verdict is notification 0x2011. insta360ctl code: it parses the direct reply to 0x56 as the verdict.
conflicts_between_sources.notification_sequence: insta360ctl: notifications use sequence 0 (TCP) or 255/unmatched (BLE). Rigacci: arbitrary bytes on TCP. Dispatch by code.
conflicts_between_sources.remote_info_uuid_base: The information characteristics 0000ffd1-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb to 0000ffd4-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb are on the Bluetooth base in pchwalek and the vendor app, and on the vendor base 3c17-d293-8e48-14fe2e4da212 in insta360ctl.
conflicts_between_sources.remote_static_values: Byte order of the 0000ce83-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb, 0000ffd3-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb and 0000ffd4-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb values differs between pchwalek (little-endian stores) and insta360ctl (listed order).
conflicts_between_sources.ui_summary_http_json: An earlier research note guessed an HTTP/JSON control API over Wi-Fi. Every source shows protobuf over TCP 6666 for control, with HTTP only for the support list and file downloads.
conflicts_between_sources.wake_beacon_layout: pchwalek and the vendor app agree; insta360ctl's layout differs.
conflicts_between_sources.x_one_ace_framing: insta360ctl: bare 16-byte header, no sync or authorization, for every non-GO model (never run on hardware). Against it: the vendor packet convention puts the total length in bytes 0-3, and the official SDK (X and ONE models only) reports BLE sync-pack (4001) and shake-hand (2207) errors.

authorization.authorization_id: A client-chosen string that identifies the client; insta360ctl sends the camera's own address string, the vendor's field comment suggests the phone's Bluetooth address. Any stable string presumably works; reuse it on every connection. Test vectors use the documentation MAC 00:00:5e:00:53:01.
authorization.cancel: CANCEL_AUTHORIZATION (40, 0x28) and CANCEL_REQUEST_AUTHORIZATION (87, 0x57) exist; no open implementation sends them.
authorization.check_authorization: Code 39 (0x27). Body: field 1 authorization_id (string), field 2 Find My token (string, optional), field 3 initiator type (0 default, 1 user, 2 app, 3 system, 16 background, 32 auto-reconnect). Reply (status 200): payload_formats.Authorization_Status.
authorization.request_authorization: Code 86 (0x56). Body: field 1 operation type (0 default, 1 pair, 2 re-pair, 3 unpair per insta360ctl's code; its prose calls 3 'force re-pair'). The camera prompts the user.

bare_header16.description: insta360ctl's assumed form for X, ONE and Ace models: the 16-byte header written directly to 0000be81-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb, with bytes 0-1 = body length (uint16 LE, header excluded), bytes 2-3 zero, the code in byte 7 only (byte 8 zero), and messages split into 20-byte writes. No sync, heartbeat or authorization. insta360ctl's prose says the two header forms produce identical bytes for small bodies; they do not (a bare empty-body header starts 00 00, the vendor form 10 00). No source ran this form on hardware.

app_string_frames.prefixes: ff 06 41 (the camera's sync prefix) and ff 0d 03 (role unknown) also appear in the string pool on their own.
app_string_frames.unknown_camera_frame: ff 06 40 08 00 08 00 00 00 b0 00 00 01 6d 90: a camera-to-app frame with packet type 0xB0 and a one-byte body 01; CRC checks; role unknown

envelope.camera_to_app: FF 06 40 ... (message), FF 06 41 ... (sync, body a repeating AB BA)
envelope.crc: CRC-16/MODBUS: reflected polynomial 0xA001, init 0xFFFF, no final xor, over every byte before the CRC, stored low byte first.
envelope.description: GO-line framing (payload_formats.Framed_Packet). Built by the vendor's native protocol library, per insta360ctl.
envelope.fragmentation: A message longer than one packet is split using the inner header's 30-bit fragment offset (bytes 10-13) and the last-fragment bit (byte 13 bit 7); the receiver concatenates fragments in offset order until the last one. In single-fragment messages the low byte of the offset field is used as the sequence number.
envelope.max_body_bytes: insta360ctl states 486 (500 - 5 - 9) in its prose and uses 495 as the maximum inner size in code; its arithmetic leaves out the 7-byte packet head, so 479 may be the true body limit. Not established.

go3_custom_service.notes: insta360ctl records a custom 128-bit service on the GO 3 with a write/notify/indicate characteristic beginning e3dd50bf, a write-only one beginning 92e86c7a and a read-only one beginning 347f7608. Only those prefixes are recorded, so the full UUIDs are unknown and nothing is declared.

notes: Code 25 returns battery level and charging state (declared as framed_get_battery_go3).
Code 16 returns 500; storage arrives only as notification 0x2010 with storage fields (payload_formats.Go3_Capture_Status).
Code 12 accepts a mode byte (see misattributed_codes).
Code 26 returns 200 for any body (no-op); code 27 returns 500.
Notifications 0x2021, 0x2025 and 0x2026 carry battery, power and periodic status and are not in the vendor table; 0x2006 and 0x200A carry capture state and device info.

codes.147: SET_WIFI_MODE (field 1 placeholder 0, field 2 mode: 0 AP, 1 station, 2 P2P)
codes.148: GET_WIFI_SCAN_LIST (field 1 interval s, field 2 count; results in notification 8249)

message_codes.description: App-to-camera codes from the vendor table, as transcribed by insta360ctl (the same codes over BLE and TCP). "hw" marks codes insta360ctl ran against a GO 3. The table continues to 201; codes 0x1000 and up are phone-request codes and 0x3000 and up factory codes.

misattributed_codes.0x0C: Sent with a raw mode byte (0 photo, 1 video, 2 timelapse, 3 HDR, 4 bullet time) to set the capture mode; works on the GO 3. The vendor table names it DELETE_FILES.
misattributed_codes.0x10: Sent as 'get storage info' (reply parsed as uint32 LE total MB, free MB, file count, formatted flag). The GO 3 answers 500. The vendor table names it SET_FILE_EXTRA.
misattributed_codes.0x12: Sent as 'get battery' on non-GO models (reply parsed as level %, uint16 LE millivolts). Untested. The vendor table names it SET_TIMELAPSE_OPTIONS.
misattributed_codes.0x28: Sent as 'get device info'. The vendor table names it CANCEL_AUTHORIZATION.
misattributed_codes.0x33: Sent with one byte as 'set HDR'. The vendor table names it START_HDR_CAPTURE.
misattributed_codes.0x37: Sent as 'power off'. The vendor table names it GET_SYNC_CAPTURE_MODE. Architecture A's power_off frame and the SDK's shutdown call (X5 and later) are the documented routes.
misattributed_codes.0x3D: Sent as 'get camera state'. The vendor table names it START_TIMESHIFT_CAPTURE.
misattributed_codes.description: insta360ctl sends these codes for meanings the vendor table does not give them, from an earlier guess at the protocol. Some work on the GO 3; on a camera that follows the table they mean something else. Do not send them outside the model they were observed on.

direct_control.wake_up_authorization: For a camera in low-power sleep the vendor library has a short frame that skips sync and protobuf: FF 0C 02, uint16 LE length, the authorization_id bytes, CRC-16/MODBUS (insta360ctl, from the native library; never sent by it). Separate from the architecture-A wake advertisement. How the camera answers is not recorded.

advertising.notes: pchwalek advertises both service UUIDs with a scan response; insta360ctl advertises the name and 0000ce80-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb only.

commands.description: Notified on 0000ce82-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb as one 9-byte value each (payload_formats.Remote_Command). pchwalek's sketch uses every one on hardware.
commands.notes: Shutter takes a photo or starts/stops a recording depending on the current mode. Screen wakes the display; pchwalek's sketch sends it twice as an off/on toggle. insta360ctl calls it "wake display".

gps_remote_emulation.description: Architecture A. The host is a BLE peripheral and GATT server that looks like an Insta360 GPS remote; the camera is the central. Sources: pchwalek's ESP32 sketch (hardware-demonstrated on an X3 and a ONE RS 1-inch) and insta360ctl's remote server (untested). Where the two disagree, pchwalek's bytes are listed first because they ran against hardware; the vendor app's string pool agrees with pchwalek wherever it can be checked.

characteristics.role: The camera writes to the remote here. What it writes is not recorded; both implementations accept and ignore it.

other_ports.notes: The research note for this spec recorded ports 8080 and 9999 in the vendor app's strings, apparently disagreeing with 6666. A re-check of the string pool did not bear that out: 8080 appears only with a private-range development address and a third-party messaging SDK's host, 9999 appears in no port-like string, and the camera address appears as http://192.168.42.1:80 and as the bare prefix http://192.168.42.1: with a port appended at run time. Port numbers compiled as integers (6666 among them) are not visible in a string pool at all, so this settles nothing either way; no second camera port is known. session: Send the sync packet; the camera echoes it (insta360ctl waits up to 5 s). Rigacci sends a keep-alive and a SET_OPTIONS right behind it without waiting.

Commands, replies and notifications as message packets; stream packets arrive while a preview runs.

station_mode_handoff.notes: SET_WIFI_CONNECTION_INFO (112) over BLE or TCP, result in notification 8232 with the new IP; after a successful join the camera drops its AP and the old TCP connection. The same protocol then runs on the new address. insta360ctl marks the flow untested and warns that some models or firmware may not support it. SET_WIFI_SEIZE_ENABLE (85) sets whether the current Wi-Fi client holds the camera exclusively (1) or can be displaced (2).

stream_packet.layout: uint32 LE total length | 01 00 00 | stream type (1 byte) | uint64 LE timestamp in microseconds | payload
stream_packet.notes: The preview is not RTSP, MJPEG or HLS, so this spec has no `camera` block; a consumer needs this bespoke stream reader.
stream_packet.start_live_stream: Code 1. Body fields (insta360ctl): 1 enable audio, 2 enable video, 4 audio sample rate (Hz), 5 audio bitrate, 6 video bitrate (Rigacci and insta360ctl send 40; unit not stated), 7 resolution, 8 enable gyro, 9 second-stream bitrate, 10 second-stream resolution, 11 number of preview streams (0 or 1), 12 enable rotate, 13 for external RTMP live. Resolution values: 9 = 1440x720 at 30 fps, 18 = 480x240 at 30 fps, 29 = 1920x1080 at 30 fps, 34 = 424x240 at 15 fps. Rigacci's ONE RS preview: video on, bitrate 40, 29, gyro on, second stream 40 and 34, one preview stream.

stream_types.0x20: video: raw H.264 or H.265 NAL units (the SDK documents H.264 with SPS/PPS; insta360ctl's GO 3 example writes H.265)

characteristics.name: Command write (app to camera)
characteristics.notes: Every command goes here, on every model; the GO 3 ignores commands written anywhere else. insta360ctl writes without response. Two command families are declared. The framed_* commands are the GO-line form: FF 07 40, uint16 LE inner size, the 16-byte inner header (uint32 LE inner size, 04 00 00, uint16 LE code, 02, sequence, 00 00, 80, 00 00), the body, then CRC-16/MODBUS (poly 0xA001 reflected, init 0xFFFF, no final xor) over everything before it, low byte first. The bare_* commands are insta360ctl's assumed X/ONE/Ace form: the 16-byte header alone, bytes 0-1 = body length (not total), code in byte 7 only, no envelope and no CRC; insta360ctl splits messages into 20-byte writes and the camera would reassemble by the length field. Only the framed family has upstream hardware results. Message bodies are protobuf, and every declared command here has an empty or fixed-size body; codes with variable bodies (authorization, Wi-Fi, options) are documented with worked examples in protocol_details.

characteristics.name: Reply and event notify (camera to app)
characteristics.notes: Replies, notifications and (GO line) the camera's sync frames. On the GO line each frame is FF 06 40 (message) or FF 06 41 (sync), uint16 LE size, inner data, CRC-16/MODBUS; a frame longer than the ATT payload spans several notifications, so accumulate until 5 + size + 2 bytes have arrived, check the CRC, then parse the 16-byte inner header (payload_formats.Inner_Header). In a reply the code field carries a status (payload_formats.Response_Status); in a notification it carries a code of 0x2000 or more (payload_formats.Notification_Codes). The byte-13 direction bit is set on camera-to-app messages (0xC0 for a single-fragment reply).

services.name: Direct-control service (architecture B)
services.notes: The camera's control service on every architecture-B model. The 16-bit value is on the Bluetooth base but is not a SIG assignment. insta360ctl's GATT table also lists Device Information (0000180a-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb) and Battery (0000180f-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb) without naming models. The GO 3 additionally exposes 0000b000-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb and 0000ae00-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb (below) and a custom 128-bit service whose full UUIDs are not recorded (protocol_details.direct_control.go3_custom_service).

What the camera sends on the three notify characteristics is not recorded. Not in the vendor app's string pool.

The only placement on a model is insta360ctl's GO 3 note, which lists 0000ae01-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb among the GO 3's write characteristics and reports that the camera ignores commands written there. What the service carries is not recorded; insta360ctl uses it only as a fallback write target. The same 16-bit numbers are JieLi's stock RCSP/OTA service on unrelated products, so the number alone proves nothing about the silicon. List it read-only; do not write to it.
